commons.title: Lone Bear, Osage, in a Fur Vest (4c506e1fecf04c15959e7021808406e0).tif
commons.credit: Vince Dillon (Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument)
commons.description:
LIBI_00312_10900; A photo postcard. This image depicts Lone Bear, an Osage. He is wearing a feathered headdress and fur vest. He holds a shield and horn club in his left hand and a feathered staff in his right. White lettering on the bottom of the image reads: “Lone Bear 101 Copyright 1912 Vince Dillon”. On the verso, a stamp in black ink along the top reads: “Vince Dillon, Photos, Fairfax, OKLA” A handwritten note along the side reads: “Osage”. This image was produced by Vince Dillon in 1912. ; photo postcard;Courtesy of the National Park Service, Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument, LIBI_00312_10900, Vince Dillon, "Lone Bear, Osage, in a Fur Vest," 1912.
Keywords: native american
commons.editorial_reason: Caption identifies Lone Bear as Osage, and he visibly wears a feathered headdress and fur vest with ceremonial objects.

commons.title: Osage Village SHS, Bedrock Features 1.jpg
commons.description: Osage Village State Historical Site, northwest of Harwood in Vernon County, Missouri.  Rock at stop along interpretive trail.  The brochure for the trail describes this stop thus: "Bedrock Features.  Notice the bedrock outcrops in this area of the site.  Signs of use by the Osage include bedrock mortars, small depressions from cracking nuts, grooves from sharpening bone tools and broad grooves from sharpening axes."
commons.editorial_reason: Osage Village attribution identifies the bedrock mortar and tool-sharpening features as Osage cultural remains.

LA FLESCHE) CHILD-NAMING RITE 55the tail of the robe are reddened to typify the glow that warns us of the ending of the day when your thoughts will again turn to the care of the little one. commons.title: Osage Nation Campus central view.jpg
commons.description: A view of the Osage Nation Campus in Pawhuska, Oklahoma.  On the left is the entrance to the Osage Nation Museum; in the center, the Osage Veterans Memorial with its distinctive feather sculpture in the center; on the right, a gazebo; in the background, the Law/Welcome Buildings.
commons.editorial_reason: Caption identifies the Osage Nation campus, whose museum and feather memorial visibly represent Osage institutional culture and architecture.

commons.title: Osage Nation Law Building.jpg
commons.description: The Law Building on the Osage National Campus in Pawhuska, Oklahoma, which houses offices for the attorney general, police department, and emergency management staff.  To the right is a portion of the Welcome Building which houses other Osage Nation government services.
commons.editorial_reason: Caption specifically identifies the Osage Nation Law Building, providing a visible architectural expression of the named people.
